# SDLC Environments & Local Resource Budget

Canonical environments for the `basketiq` workspace. All development happens from the local macOS machine.

| Environment | Host | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Local | macOS (this machine) | Editing, commits, tests, builds, `gh`, `gcloud`, triggering GitHub Actions |
| Self-hosted runners | `development` (Mac mini), `integration2` | Execute GitHub Actions jobs via the `pick-runner` pattern (see `06-github-actions-runners.md`). Not general-purpose shells — do not treat them as remote dev environments |
| Staging (data) | GCP `spain-nextgen-staging` (Firestore + GCS) | `BIQ_ENV=staging` data environment |
| Staging (services) | GCP `spain-nextgen-staging` (Cloud Run, `europe-west1`) | Always-on staging services; deployed only via workflows, never by hand |
| Production | GCP + GitHub Actions | Public site and services; automated deploys only |

## Git on Local

- **Fetch/pull**: HTTPS (`https://github.com/BasketIQ/<repo>.git`) with `gh` as credential helper.
- **Push**: SSH over 443 via the `github-basketiq` alias (`ssh.github.com:443`), configured in `~/.ssh/config`.
- **gh CLI**: installed and authenticated on Local. Run it directly — do not proxy it through other hosts.

## Operational budget

Local is the execution host. The only active IDE workspace is `basketiq` (`/Users/jjdelcampo/projects/basketiq`); all repos live under it.

### Allowed on Local

- Read, edit, commit and push files.
- `git`, `gh`, `gcloud` directly.
- Builds, tests, watchers and dev servers.

### Workspace budget

- Generated artifacts, caches, venvs, logs and heavy outputs must be `.gitignore`d or outside the language server's active set.
- No `venv`, `.pytest_cache`, `node_modules`, `dist`, Allure report, dump, export or backup may become live input to the language server.
- If a command can block the session (watchers, servers, long tests), use a `timeout` or run it in the background.

### Remote runtime budget

Remote services (Cloud Run, GCS) have RAM/CPU/concurrency budgets. Any repo with Cloud Run services or dedicated runners must declare its budget in the owning repo.

- Cloud Run limits, store connection pools, E2E timeouts and runner circuit breakers must be versioned values, not persistent manual console tweaks.
- Any increase of memory, CPU, concurrency, max instances or connection pools requires a PR with cause, validation and rollback.

### Non-compliance signals

- Language server RAM grows from indexing caches or heavy artifacts.
- More than one local server/watch running without explicit justification.
- A local command leaves the chat blocked.
- Heavy untracked outputs appear in `git status` mixed with working files.

### Corrective action

1. Stop the process causing pressure.
2. Exclude or move the outputs triggering indexing out of the active workspace.
3. If the case repeats, add a specific rule or workflow in `basketiq-wow`.

### RAM-safe close checklist

- Confirm no watchers, servers or local processes remain alive.
- Review `git status` to ensure no caches, heavy logs or generated outputs are being committed.
- If RAM pressure was detected, document cause and corrective action before continuing.

## No Direct Production Deployments

**NEVER deploy to production directly from Local.**

Every production deploy MUST go through GitHub Actions workflows.

### Allowed

- `gh workflow run <workflow>.yml -R <org>/<repo> --ref main` — trigger a GH Actions run from Local.
- `gh run watch <run_id> -R <org>/<repo>` — monitor a run from Local.

### Forbidden (deployment)

- `gcloud storage rsync dist/ gs://...` to production.
- `scp` / `rsync` to any production bucket or server.
- Any direct upload to production outside CI.

## Google Cloud authentication

If a `gcloud` command fails due to expired credentials or asks for re-authentication, do not stop; re-authenticate and retry.

### Automatic re-authentication

```bash
basket gcloud-auth --local
```

The command uses Playwright to complete the OAuth flow without opening a browser. It requires credentials: the canonical file is `basketiq-wow/cfg/basketiq/gcloud-auth.config.json` (gitignored; see `gcloud-auth.config.example.json`). If that file does not exist, ask the user or use `--password-env`, `--password-file` (chmod 600) or `--password-stdin` (only when a user is present). Never write the password in chat or in versioned files.

### Application Default Credentials (ADC)

If the error mentions `application-default login` and the context is non-interactive, prefer `gcloud auth print-access-token` over ADC. If ADC must actually be refreshed, run `basket gcloud-auth --local` first, then `gcloud auth application-default login` in an interactive session if still needed.

### After re-authenticating

Re-run the original `gcloud` command that failed and continue the task.

## Scope

This rule applies to the entire `basketiq` IDE workspace and takes precedence over any project-specific rule. Project rules may add restrictions, never relax them.
